label: Digitally Immersed & Emotionally Distressed
summary: This profile represents highly educated women who spend more than five hours daily online and report elevated levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety. Their UCLA-8 loneliness score (mean 1.69), PHQ-9 depression score (mean 1.75), and GAD-7 anxiety score (mean 2.16) all sit in the higher range, suggesting a co-occurring pattern of emotional distress. With 170 respondents in this cluster, the profile points to a consistent association between heavy digital engagement and compounded psychological burden among graduate-educated females.
demographic_anchor: Female, graduate-level education or above, daily screen time exceeding 5 hours
behavior_markers: Heavy daily digital engagement (more than 5 hours)
Higher anxiety levels relative to other emotional distress indicators
Pattern consistent with social isolation despite online presence

label: Well-Adjusted Male Graduate
summary: This profile represents respondents who report notably low levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms. With mean scores near the floor on all three validated scales (UCLA-8, PHQ-9, GAD-7), these individuals appear to be functioning well psychologically and do not exhibit clinically meaningful distress on any measured dimension.
demographic_anchor: Male, holding a graduate degree or above, reporting 1–3 hours of daily screen time or social media use
behavior_markers: Very low loneliness scores (UCLA-8 mean ≈ 0.75), indicating strong perceived social connectedness
Minimal depressive symptomatology (PHQ-9 mean ≈ 0.35), well below clinical thresholds
Near-zero anxiety symptoms (GAD-7 mean ≈ 0.02), suggesting negligible worry or tension
Moderate and bounded screen time (1–3 hours), consistent with disciplined digital habits
Higher educational attainment, which may correlate with greater access to social and professional networks
tone: Stable, composed, and socially connected with an overall sense of psychological well-being

label: Well-Adjusted Male Graduate
summary: This profile represents respondents who report consistently low levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms. With mean scores well below clinical thresholds on all three validated scales (UCLA-8 loneliness ≈ 1.24, PHQ-9 depression ≈ 0.79, GAD-7 anxiety ≈ 0.83), these individuals demonstrate robust psychological well-being across emotional and social dimensions.
demographic_anchor: Male, holding a graduate degree or above, reporting 1–3 hours of daily screen/internet use
behavior_markers: Reports minimal feelings of social isolation or disconnection (UCLA-8 mean ≈ 1.24)
Exhibits very low depressive symptomatology (PHQ-9 mean ≈ 0.79, well below mild threshold)
Displays very low anxiety symptomatology (GAD-7 mean ≈ 0.83, well below mild threshold)
Maintains moderate and limited daily screen or internet use (1–3 hours)
Demonstrates a pattern of emotional stability across all measured psychological domains
